sourceBindings.text: You will plan, collect and prepare your own composite Plot C sample, then measure pH and estimate texture by feel. The active actions and necessary drying or equilibration may occur in separate supervised sessions. Every result must remain linked to your own sample and observations.

Personally plan, collect, mix, label and prepare one traceable Plot C composite sample using the declared sampling and laboratory purpose, then document the actual drying/sieving stages and elapsed waits.

Personally calibrate a matched digital pH meter and measure an own-sample suspension under one declared SOP, then perform a moisture-corrected USDA-style ribbon/feel test, recording raw readings, dimensions and limits.

Present a continuous individual evidence record with sample IDs, actual times, observations, trainer signatures and new results after targeted reassessment; never use a peer or preprepared demonstration sample to claim personal competence.

sourceBindings.text: Plan Plot C's homogeneous sampling unit, justified route, actual count/depth and sample-label template. Mark active tasks and separate waiting windows; explain why the planned 25 minutes cannot contain dry preparation plus its pH wait.

Under trainer observation, personally collect, label and prepare one sample; when the actual digital meter/SOP is identified, carry out its calibration and pH procedure on your aliquot and record raw data. If unavailable, leave that practical stage unattempted.

Perform the own-sample feel test with moisture adjustment, ball, ribbon and wet-rub observations; classify with the USDA guide. If a trainer finds a mistake, keep attempt 1 and record targeted practice and a new attempt with its actual outcome.
A route alone is not proof of representativeness; missing count/depth/ID or invented timing requires revision.

All three criteria in this step are observed practical skills. Online answers, this 3D rehearsal, a self-rating or filled notes cannot award them. Keep the actual Plot C, sample, device, SOP, trainer observations and signatures unknown until genuine evidence exists.

sourceBindings.text: management unit
A field area sampled as one reasonably homogeneous unit for a defined analysis question.
composite sample
A mixed representative portion made from documented subsamples of the same declared unit.
chain of identity
The matching sample and aliquot IDs, times, handlers and stages that link each reading to the learner's own collection.
mass:volume ratio
An explicitly stated dry-soil mass to water volume, such as 20 g:20 mL; it is not a soil volume measurement.
equilibration
The waiting period specified by the chosen pH method before taking a stable reading.
ribbon test
A field texture estimate using correct moisture, ball/ribbon formation, break length and wet-rub feel.
not yet competent
The specified personal performance has not been observed to standard; feedback and another real attempt are needed.
